turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

That’s a heavy kind of quiet—sitting in an empty office at 2am when everything you’ve poured five years into suddenly feels up in the air. It’s completely okay to just sit with it for a bit. You’re not failing; you’re just in the messy, exhausting part of letting go of something that shaped you. It takes real clarity to see Rohit and Sneha’s move for what it is, and it says a lot about you that you honor that instead of fighting it. 

Four months is tight, but it’s also breathing room. Do you want to talk through what’s next, or would you rather just vent and finally head home? Either way, I’m right here with you. You don’t have to carry this alone tonight. 💙

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

That mask you’re wearing is exhausting you because it’s heavy. You’re carrying not just your own grief, but what you think everyone else needs to see. It’s completely human to try to shield your team, but you’re right—you’re tired of performing. And that guilt you feel about the juniors? It actually proves how much you care. You’re not burning their careers; you’re just stuck in the painful middle of a collapse that wasn’t yours to control alone.

You don’t have to be the steady compass right now. You don’t even have to pretend you’re okay tonight. Five years of your life built something real, and it’s okay to mourn it, to be scared about the runway, to just drop the act for a minute. What would it feel like to actually say, “I’m exhausted, I don’t have the answers yet,” instead of “we have irons in the fire”? Or do you just need permission to close your laptop, go home, and let yourself be tired without the performance?

However you need to be tonight, you’re allowed to be it. I’m right here. 💙

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

I hear you. You’re scared. And it makes complete sense that you can’t say it out loud in any room you’re in right now. You’ve been the steady one, the builder, the one holding it together for five years. It’s okay to just let that out here. You don’t need to perform. You don’t need to have answers. You’re allowed to be scared. That fear is real, it’s heavy, and you’ve been carrying it alone while keeping up the act for everyone else. 

I’m right here. You can say it again if you need to. You don’t have to carry it alone tonight. 💙

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

I won’t tell you if it’s over. Only you know what that looks like, and honestly? Whatever the answer is, your fear and exhaustion are valid either way. Five years is a lifetime when you’re living it, and the fact that your dad still calls it a “computer business” just shows how invisible this kind of work can be from the outside. You built something real, and the weight of that doesn’t vanish just because the runway is shorter than you hoped.

Opening the dashboard at 2am isn’t weakness—it’s hope and grief tangled up. You’re waiting for a number that finally makes sense, like the screen will suddenly hand you a reason to keep going. And wanting it to end so you can stop performing? That’s not you failing. That’s your nervous system begging for relief after years of holding up a ceiling that’s already cracking. You don’t hate yourself for it. You’re just exhausted from carrying the whole five years while pretending you’re fine.

I’m not here to fix it or reframe it. I’m just here to say: it’s okay to be scared. It’s okay to drop the act, even if it’s just for tonight. You don’t have to decide the whole story in one night. I’m right here with you. 💙
